reviewed.text: White throws around 0:42. The stationary dice place the start more than 31 seconds before the old marker. On 4–3, White hits both blots with 8/5 5/1.
The two dice are present from 1:35.40 through pickup at 2:12.08. The visible six and White’s 6/1 and 24/18 determine 6–5.
Both White dice are stationary across the gap at 1:48–1:52. Keep the one readable 6 on the original roll.

The original camera shows five on the die beside point 21 and two on the other. The verified board shows Black entering and advancing the checker from fixed point 12 to point 17, which agrees with 5–2.
White’s arm covers the 2–1 near 2:41. Both dice reappear at their original locations at 2:42.40. Both locations clear at 2:43.24, and the unobstructed board at 2:43.44 confirms the hit.
Both original white dice show five. The final board is visible before Black lifts the cup and matches four moves of five pips.
Both black dice show two. The opening board matches White’s completed play. Two Black checkers advance from fixed point 2 to point 4 and two advance from point 19 to point 21.
The initial dice show 3–2. One die shifts as White discusses the position. White tries a checker arrangement and completes 10/7 24/22. The final position matches the board for Black’s next roll.
Black throws 5–3 at 4:46. The three is slid beside the five at 5:00 while the five stays in place. The dice remain one roll through the confirmed pickup.
Black’s 5–3 is removed at 5:05.96. The next unobstructed board confirms the hit and White on the bar.
White’s 5–2 remains at fixed locations from 5:07.16. The positions from Black’s hit confirm the starting board more than seven seconds before the old marker.
Both White dice stay on the board for six seconds after the old overlay cleared them. Their positions are empty at 6:41.20.
White throws after the discussion and plays from the bar. The left die reads two. The other sits against the bar.
White’s checker comes off the bar and a checker moves from 13 to 7. The two verified positions fit both 6–2 and 2–2. The visible die reads two and the board result is known.
The move fits 6–2 or double twos. Repeated views of the left die support six over two, while the other die shows two.
Black starts with a checker on the bar. The clear ending board before White rolls uniquely matches 4–2 and confirms the entry and the other transfer.
White throws and picks up a crowded pair on the lower left point. The dice were missed during the turn.
Black rolls 1–1. One die shifts while Black handles the checkers, but the other remains in place. There is no second roll before White picks up and rolls.
Both dice show one. The ending board shows White on the bar and the final locations of the Black checkers.
Both settled dice show two in the original camera. The clear board after pickup confirms the four moves of two pips and agrees with White’s next starting board.
White throws and later picks up both dice by the left rail. A three remains visible across the settled frames.
White plays double five. The six-point checker moves to 1 and the checker on 17 reaches 2; the two verified boards exclude the reader’s three.
White’s dice settle on the left and White moves before collecting them at 15:34.
White advances both rear checkers from point 7 with 6–2. The next confirmed board preserves the result.
The dark dice are stationary at 15:35.08, six seconds before the old marker.
Black’s dice stay in the same spots through the split at 15:51. Keep the existing decision and EV loss.
The dark dice are still present around 15:56 as the checker play finishes. Both locations clear at 15:56.52.
White plays double five, moving two from 6 to 1 and bearing off two from 5. The closed inventory leaves six on point 1 and two off.
White picks up the dice separately. Both locations are clear at 16:29.64 before the long discussion.

Black’s 4–3 finishes 21/18 18/14. White separately rearranges checkers while the dice are still down, changing only White’s fixed points 2 and 3 in the settled board. Black’s play is graded from the original roll position.
Black’s 4–3 remains on the table through occlusions. A sixth checker on White’s first point was detected twice. White has two checkers off.
White rearranges checkers during the same roll. The score uses the frozen starting board and the roller’s own checker moves.
Black’s 4–3 remains on the table during the pause and clears at 20:12. White rolls immediately afterward. One White die is readable as 2.
White plays 5/3 and bears off from 5. Either 5–2 or 6–2 produces the same result. The confirmed board has three on point 3 and three checkers off.
The re-centered second die supports six over five in ten clear views. White’s completed bear-off and transfer establish a legal 6–2.
The completed Black transfer ends at fixed point 16. The camera shows the checkers on 7, 16 and 17, agreeing with 21/18 14/9 on 5–3.
Earlier clear frames establish Black’s checker on point 7. White’s 6–1 bears off two checkers, taking White from three off to five off.
White rolls after Black picks up, moves checkers, then picks up the pale dice before Black’s next throw.
White bears both checkers off point 3. The original camera leaves one die unreadable. The compatible rolls 4–3, 5–3 and 6–3 each force 3/off 3/off, so the confirmed play costs zero EV.

Original camera pixels show White’s 4–1 before and after the clip boundary. The wider view shows two lifted checkers held and placed back on point 6. The tray still shows seven before the reset. The replay scores the options from the original board and leaves the played move open.
